## My Thinking

I farm in Quzhou. The answer is what it's always been — winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground. Every year. That rotation fits our climate, our soils, our equipment, and our buyers. I've got 20 mu I work myself, and I rented another 5 mu from a neighbor who moved to the city, so 25 mu total.

I went to agricultural university in the 1990s and I've been doing this for nearly 20 years. I know what grows here. The North China Plain is wheat-maize country. Our precipitation is too low and poorly timed for rice, vegetables need more labor and capital than I have right now, and cotton prices have been terrible for years. Wheat and maize — that's what the grain station wants, that's what I know how to do.

For wheat I'll plant Jimai 22 — proven variety, good scab resistance, high yield. For maize I'll use Xianyu 335 hybrid, same as last year. No reason to change what works.

On fertilizer: I'm going to be a little more careful with nitrogen this year. The county agricultural bureau keeps pushing soil testing and I had mine done last autumn. My fields are slightly high in phosphorus already from years of compound fertilizer. I'll cut phosphorus a bit on the maize, heavier nitrogen split-applied.

Water is always my worry. The government is cracking down on groundwater pumping — they've been reducing our electricity subsidy for irrigation. I'll do three irrigations for wheat: pre-winter, jointing, and heading. For maize I'll try to get by on rainfall and one emergency irrigation if the tasseling period is dry. I have a low-pressure pipe irrigation system I installed five years ago.

Pest management: wheat gets herbicide in winter, a fungicide spray around heading to prevent fusarium, and one aphid spray in May. Maize gets pre-emergence herbicide and I'll scout for corn borer in July — spray if I see damage exceeding threshold.

Tillage: rotary after maize harvest in October to prepare the wheat seedbed. After wheat in June I'll do no-tillage direct seeding for maize — the window between harvest and optimal maize planting is only a few days and I can't afford to lose it to tillage.
